newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse Feb turnover 1.8 pct down mo/mo.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse Feb turnover 1.8 pct down mo/mo.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) February turnover fell to 134.307 million dinars ($23.81 million) from 136.796 million in January, the bourse said on Tuesday.
The number of deals rose to 697 from 619 a month ago.
"February turnover is down on the same month last year, but the structure of turnover has changed," BSE general manager Pava Zecevic told reporters.
The BSE said its turnover stood at 155.88 million dinars in 461 deals in February 1996.
Unlike early 1996 when the bourse turnover was dominated by the central bank short-term bonds, commercial papers were dominant in the early 1997 market activity.
Commercial paper segment accounted for 59 percent of the February turnover with 594 deals worth 79.799 million dinars.
Treasury bills followed with 74 deals totalling 10.22 million dinars.

The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) 30-day bonds, auctioned in February only once, accounted for 9.4 million dinars or a modest seven percent of the total monthly turnover. The bank offered a 20-million dinar tranche for sale.
Wheat contracts, relaunched in mid-February, fetched only four percent of the monthly total against 27 percent in January.
Low buying interest followed after the Serbian Commodity Reserve Agency, the issuer of contracts, decided to abandon payment in instalments and accept only cash settlement.
According to BSE figures, shares accounted for 29.496 million dinars or 22 percent of the February total. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
